title: A browser reads the page, and the reading is the check
summary: Build one script that opens the Karta Watch page in a real browser, reads the boxes and computed styles the browser actually resolved, and prints them as one JSON document. It builds the instrument and nothing else — no layout defect is fixed here and no page rule is changed. The work that uses it is a later binder, written against a tool that already exists.
motivation:
The page carries 258 self-test checks and every one reads a DECLARED stylesheet value. The defect that started this work is legal in all 258: `body{display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center}` (skills/karta-status/scripts/serve_status.py:1449-1456) is a legal declaration, and in a column flexbox `align-items` governs the horizontal axis, so the app root is sized to its contents and the column's width cap never binds. Nothing declared is wrong. What the browser resolved is wrong. A declaration check cannot see that, and adding more declaration checks will never make it able to.

This binder exists because the previous attempt built the instrument and used it in one plan. Eight items, three adversarial review rounds, 41 findings — and roughly a third of each later round's findings were defects introduced by hand-patching the round before. The cause was structural rather than careless: seven items carried assertions about a tool that did not exist yet, so every claim was a cross-reference to a specification instead of a statement about a thing. Change the specification in one field and several other fields quietly became false.

So the instrument is planned alone. Three items, one new file, one runbook section. Nothing here says “a later item will” — that sentence is the coupling the split removed. The measurement groups later work will pin are not written here and the registry ships empty on purpose: `--check all` over an empty registry exits 1 and says why, which is the correct answer rather than a hole.

Three defects the reviews found in the earlier harness specification are corrected here rather than carried forward, and each is written into the item that owns it. The harness cannot ask for port 0, because serve_status.py announces the port it was ASKED for and not the one it bound. The PATH used to prove the floor stays browser-free did not reliably remove the browser. And the fidelity runbook still tells a reader to point an automated capture at a `file://` URL, which the browser this harness drives refuses outright.

included: skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py — NEW, and the only new file in this binder. PEP 723 header, stdlib only, argparse, a --self-test mode over embedded fixtures, in the same house pattern as every other script under skills/*/scripts/. It boots serve_status.py as a subprocess against a caller-given fixture root, drives playwright-cli as a subprocess to reach named viewports and named states, reads getComputedStyle and getBoundingClientRect off the live DOM, and prints one JSON document on stdout.

its two generated Codex mirrors, .agents/skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py and plugins/karta/skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py, regenerated with `uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py` and byte-identical to the canonical file.

the gate modes. `--check <group>` compares readings against a named group of expected values carried inside the script; `--check all` runs every named group. Both exit 1 rather than pass when they cannot do the job they were asked to do.
the empty group registry, which is a decision and not an omission. A group states what a page SHOULD measure, which is a claim about a fix, and no fix lands here.

the floor rule, decided here rather than discovered later: the script's --self-test is pure — no browser, no network, no server subprocess — and it joins the floor with no validator edit, because scripts/validate_plugin.py:1348-1354 already sweeps every skills/*/scripts/*.py and self-tests each one through _run_self_test (validate_plugin.py:1298-1330). A browser measurement is never in the floor. `uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test` must stay green on a machine with no playwright-cli and no node at all.

the skip behaviour, the one behaviour with an exit code of its own: with no playwright-cli on PATH a measurement run prints one loud line naming every viewport and state it did not take, and exits 3 — neither 0 nor 1.

docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md — one new section naming the script by path, the command, the three state names, the three exit codes and the skip line; plus a correction to the instruction at line 28, which tells a reader to point an automated capture at a `file://` URL that playwright-cli refuses.

the runtime floor, and the cost of setting it. node joins python in runtime_contract because playwright-cli needs it: @playwright/cli 0.1.15 declares engines.node >=18 in its own package.json and the toolchain on the planning host is v24.18.0. This repository pins no node version anywhere — no .nvmrc, no package.json, no .tool-versions — so the floor is read from the tool's own engines field rather than from a pin file that does not exist. Say the cost plainly, because runtime_contract is binder-wide and on_unavailable is halt: on a machine with no node, karta-build halts at preflight and none of the three items build, including the two that need only python. That is deliberate. Two of three items are parts of a browser-measurement tool whose only purpose is the third item's proof, so building two-thirds of an instrument and stopping is a worse outcome than halting once with the reason named. The alternative was worse in a quieter way: without the declaration, the third item's oracle on a browserless machine exits 3, the && chain fails, and karta-verify reads a missing browser as a failing check — a false defect signal pointed at code that is fine.

one real measurement run against the committed fixture docs/designs/fixtures/watch-fidelity-state, so the instrument leaves this binder proven against a rendered page and not only against its own embedded fixtures.
excluded: every layout fix. Not one page rule changes here. The content-sized column at serve_status.py:1449-1456 is the defect that motivated the instrument and it is left exactly as it stands — measuring it is this binder's product, repairing it is later work.

skills/karta-status/scripts/serve_status.py, in every form. The harness boots it as a subprocess and never imports it, never edits it, and never edits its mirrors. That includes the tempting one-line change described under measure-page-harness — making the non-hub path announce httpd.server_port rather than the port it was asked for. It is a real improvement and it is still not made here; the port_discovery clause of that item says why.
any measurement group carrying real expected numbers, for the reason given in scope.included.

type: visual oracles. Every oracle here is type unit, dispositioned by karta-verify against the diff. karta-validate's serve_design.py roots its server at the design file's own parent (skills/karta-validate/scripts/serve_design.py:73), so this repo's eight woff2 faces and its mascot — referenced from the committed capture as ../../skills/karta-status/assets/ — all 404, and any type reading taken through it is taken against fallback faces. A separate binder, design-gate-serves-its-own-assets, repairs that; nothing here waits on it or depends on it.

comparing the page against the design. This harness reads ONE side, the served page. Serving the design capture so a browser can reach its own assets is a different job; the only trace of it here is a runbook correction telling a reader not to take a route that does not work.
the dark theme, the design's second breakpoint, and the 27 design tokens. No token value is added, changed or removed, and no theme other than the runbook's pinned ?theme=light is measured.
provisioning anything. The harness installs no browser, no node, no python. It detects what is present, uses it, and says plainly when it is not.

a shared_terms block. Three items, one new file, and the single string that must match across two different files — the skip line — is asserted directly by the item that copies it, with a negative control. A shared term that nothing writes stops a delivery at its final wave, and no term here is worth that risk.

design_facts.stack: Python stdlib scripts shipped as a Claude Code plugin and a Codex CLI plugin; the page under measurement is a single-file Vue global-build app served by serve_status.py

work_items.title: Read the rendered page in a real browser and print one document
work_items.summary: Add skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py: it boots the page against a given fixture root, drives playwright-cli to reach named viewports and three named states, reads getComputedStyle and getBoundingClientRect, and prints one JSON document — or, with no browser on PATH, prints one loud skip line and exits 3.

contract.exposes: one stdlib-only script in the house pattern — inline PEP 723 metadata with `dependencies = []`, argparse, and a --self-test mode printing [PASS]/[FAIL] lines. Its whole command surface after this item is three flags: `--root <dir>`, the fixture root a measurement run serves; `--viewport <WxH>`, repeatable, default 1440x900; and `--self-test`. There is deliberately no --port flag — the harness always probes its own port, so no caller can hand it a port another process is already holding, and no wave has to reason about which port belongs to whom. A measurement run prints ONE JSON document on stdout for the whole run, never one per probe, so a reader quotes a single artifact. Its top level is exactly three keys, and later work may rely on them and on the key names inside them. `run`: `root`, `port`, `viewports`, `browser` (the playwright-cli version string) — and no wall-clock timestamp, so two runs over an unchanged tree differ only where the page differs. `states`: a map of the three state names to an object of `reached` (boolean) and `reason` (a string when reached is false, null when it is true). `probes`: a list, each entry with `state`, `viewport`, `selector`, `computed` (the getComputedStyle values read) and `rect` (the getBoundingClientRect box). The three state names are fixed here and are the two clicks the runbook already calls protocol (docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md:30-35): `at-rest`, `binder-panel-open`, `card-detail-open`. Exit codes: 0 measured, 1 the run failed, 3 no browser. Two module-level constants are part of the exposed surface so a checker can read them instead of re-typing them: `SKIP_LINE`, the exact string the no-browser path prints, and `STATES`, the three state names in order. Importing the module has no side effects — argparse and every subprocess sit under `if __name__ == "__main__"` — so reading either constant costs nothing and starts nothing.
contract.consumes: serve_status.py and playwright-cli, both as subprocesses, and a committed fixture root passed with --root. It imports neither and edits neither.
contract.port_discovery: the harness picks a concrete free port itself: it binds a socket to 127.0.0.1 port 0, reads the number the kernel assigned, closes the socket, and passes that number to serve_status.py as --port <n>. It does NOT pass 0. Passing 0 cannot work, and this is the correction to the earlier specification: serve_status.py builds its announced URL from the port it was ASKED for — `port = args.port if args.port is not None else 8765` then `url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/"` (serve_status.py:15977-15980) — so a server started with --port 0 announces http://127.0.0.1:0/ and nothing downstream can learn what it actually bound. Only the multi-repo hub path reads the bound socket (serve_status.py:5252-5256, `httpd.server_port`); the plain serving path never does. Two fixes were available and the cheaper one is taken. Changing serve_status.py to announce httpd.server_port on the plain path is one line and arguably better, and it is refused here for a reason that will not age: serve_status.py is a 16,000-line file that the sibling column-fidelity work edits in several places, and an edit here would collide with all of them for a benefit the harness can give itself. The cost of picking the port outside the server is a race — between closing the probe socket and serve_status.py binding it, another process can take the number — and it is handled rather than hoped away: on a server that fails to come up the harness probes a fresh port and retries, up to five attempts, and if all five fail it exits 1 naming the ports it tried. It never prints a partial document and never falls back to a port it did not verify. It also never reuses a server it did not start, because a leftover server may be rooted at a different fixture and would answer with the wrong page.
contract.browser_probe_order: the browser is probed BEFORE the server is started, so a skipped run starts no subprocess at all and leaves nothing to clean up. That ordering is what makes exit 3 cheap and makes the skip line honest — it can name every viewport and state without having taken any.
contract.preserves: the floor stays browser-free. python remains the only runtime that `scripts/` and `skills/*/scripts/` need for --self-test. The validator invokes each script as `sys.executable <script> --self-test` and first requires --self-test to appear in its --help output (validate_plugin.py:1298-1330), so the script must run correctly under a plain system python3 with no uv and no third-party import, and must list --self-test in --help. Nothing about the page changes: no rule, no token, no behaviour, no entry in selftest_behaviours.txt.
contract.regression_risk: the sharp edge is a check that goes green when it could not run. If a missing browser produced exit 0 and an empty document, later work would gate on nothing while looking measured — worse than the declaration-only floor this instrument is meant to supplement, because it would carry the appearance of measurement. So the skip path gets its own exit code, its own assertion and its own failing companion. The mirror-image risk is a self-test that needs a browser, which would drag the whole repo floor into needing one; both directions are asserted, in opposite senses. A third, quieter risk is a run that leaves a server or a browser session alive and poisons the next run, so teardown is asserted rather than assumed.

oracle.command: uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --self-test && python3 skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --self-test && python3 skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --help | grep -q -- --self-test && SHIM=$(mktemp -d) && ln -s "$(command -v uv)" "$SHIM/uv" && ln -s "$(command -v python3)" "$SHIM/python3" && env PATH="$SHIM:/usr/bin:/bin" sh -c 'command -v uv >/dev/null && command -v python3 >/dev/null && ! command -v playwright-cli >/dev/null' && env PATH="$SHIM:/usr/bin:/bin" uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test && sh -c 'env PATH="$1:/usr/bin:/bin" uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --root docs/designs/fixtures/watch-fidelity-state; test $? -eq 3' _ "$SHIM" && uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test && uv run scripts/check_shared_copies.py --self-test && uv run scripts/sync_codex_agents.py --check && uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check
assertions: a measurement run boots serve_status.py on a port the harness itself probed and verified, rooted at the --root the caller gave, waits for the page to answer, drives playwright-cli to set each named viewport and reach each named state, and prints exactly one JSON document on stdout carrying every probe's getComputedStyle values and getBoundingClientRect box. One document for the whole run, never one per probe.

the document's top level is exactly the three keys `run`, `states` and `probes`, with the contents the contract names, and it carries no wall-clock timestamp — so two runs against the same tree produce byte-identical output wherever the page has not changed. The failing companion: a run that emits a second top-level key, or a run whose two invocations over an unchanged tree differ, fails the self-test.

the three states are `at-rest`, `binder-panel-open` and `card-detail-open`, the two clicks the runbook already calls protocol (docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md:30-35). A state the run could not reach is reported with reached false and a named reason, never as an empty reading — the fixture binder derives as next and only the current binder's panel is open at rest (serve_status.py:3671-3673, isOpen returns key === 'now' when the reader has decided nothing), so the work-item cards are absent from the DOM until the first click and an unreached state is a normal outcome that has to read as one. The failing companion: a probe whose state was never reached and which reports a value anyway fails.

with playwright-cli absent from PATH the harness prints the line `SKIPPED — no browser: playwright-cli is not on PATH, so no rendered geometry was measured and nothing below is proven` byte for byte, then names every viewport and every state it did not take, and exits 3 — a code distinct from 0 (measured) and from 1 (ran and something failed). It never prints a measurement it did not take and it never exits 0 on that path. The failing companion: a fixture run in which the skip path returns 0, or returns 1, or prints a probe value, fails.
the browser is probed before the server is started: on the skip path no serve_status.py subprocess is spawned at all. The failing companion is a fixture in which a skipped run spawns the server.

the harness never asks serve_status.py for port 0. It binds 127.0.0.1 port 0 itself, reads the assigned number, closes the socket and passes that concrete number as --port. On a server that does not come up it retries with a freshly probed port up to five times, then exits 1 naming every port it tried. The failing companions: a fixture where the harness passes 0 through to the server fails; and a fixture where every bind attempt is refused must exit 1 with the port list, never exit 0 and never hang.

--self-test runs with no browser, no network and no server subprocess, covers document assembly, the probe grammar, the three states, the skip path, the port-probe retry and all three exit codes over embedded fixtures, prints [PASS]/[FAIL] lines, and exits 0 under a plain `python3 skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --self-test` with no uv involved. `--self-test` also appears in --help, which the validator requires before it will run the mode at all (validate_plugin.py:1298-1330).

the whole repo floor stays green on a browserless machine, proven rather than asserted. The proof does not subtract a guessed directory from PATH — that is what the earlier specification did, and it failed silently, because a `uv tool install`ed playwright-cli lands in the same directory as uv and survived the removal. Instead the run allow-lists: it creates an empty directory, symlinks only uv and python3 into it, and sets PATH to that directory plus /usr/bin and /bin. Under that PATH the run confirms all three facts before trusting it — `command -v uv` resolves, `command -v python3` resolves, and `command -v playwright-cli` resolves to nothing — and only then runs `uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test`, which must pass. The failing companion, which proves the probe can see a browser when one is there rather than always reporting absence: the self-test plants an executable named playwright-cli in a temporary directory, confirms `command -v playwright-cli` finds it when that directory is on PATH, and confirms the allow-listed PATH does not.
under that same allow-listed PATH a measurement run exits 3, which is the skip path exercised against a genuinely browserless environment rather than against a fixture that only describes one.

the harness writes nothing into the repository. It prints to stdout; its only side effects are the server subprocess it starts and the playwright-cli session it opens, and it stops both on every exit path including the failure paths. A run that leaves either alive fails its own teardown check, which is asserted rather than assumed. The failing companion is a fixture in which teardown is skipped.

importing measure_page.py as a module runs nothing: no argparse, no subprocess, no server, no browser probe. It exposes `SKIP_LINE` and `STATES` as module-level constants holding exactly what the run prints and reaches, so a checker elsewhere reads the strings rather than keeping a second copy. The failing companion is a fixture that imports the module and asserts nothing was spawned and nothing was printed.

the script is stdlib-only with inline PEP 723 metadata declaring `dependencies = []`, uses argparse, and reaches serve_status.py and playwright-cli through subprocess rather than importing either — the page's own module must stay importable without a browser dependency anywhere near it.

the regenerated Codex mirrors under .agents/skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py and plugins/karta/skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py are byte-identical to the canonical file, and `uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check` is clean.

signals: not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated.

capability or resource escalation — a new script that starts a server subprocess and drives a browser. Nothing else in this repo does either. It is picked up by the floor automatically because _check_skill_scripts sweeps skills/*/scripts/*.py (validate_plugin.py:1348-1354), which is why the pure-self-test rule is not optional: the moment the file lands, every commit in this repo runs its --self-test.

contract mutation — the harness fixes the three state names and the document's three top-level keys, and later work will read them. That is stated in exposes rather than discovered by a reader of the code.
explicit — this is the whole architectural bet of the binder. If it is cut, nothing else here has a reason to exist.
scope of impact — the new script is swept by the repo floor from its first commit, so a defect in its --self-test blocks every commit in the repository until fixed, not just this binder's.

work_items.title: Turn a reading into a gate that cannot pass by accident
work_items.summary: Add --check <group> and --check all to the harness: compare measured readings against a named group of expected values carried in the script, print one line per comparison, and exit 1 — never 0 with a printed complaint — whenever the comparison cannot be made or does not hold.

contract.exposes: two modes on measure_page.py. `--check <group>` takes the measurements, compares each reading against that group's expected value, prints one line per comparison naming the selector, the property, the expected value and the measured value, and exits 0 only when every comparison holds. `--check all` resolves every group in the registry and exits 1 if any group fails or if the registry names nothing. Plus the registry itself: a single named table inside the script, holding zero groups when this item is done.
contract.ordering: the order in which failures are decided is fixed here, because it is exactly the kind of detail two later items would otherwise each assume differently. A configuration fault is decided FIRST, before the browser is probed and before any server starts: an unknown group name exits 1, a group whose expectation list is empty exits 1, and `--check all` over an empty registry exits 1. Only once the request resolves to at least one non-empty group does the run probe the browser — and there, a missing playwright-cli exits 3 with the skip line and claims no comparison in either direction. So the two exit codes never contend: 1 means the harness knew what was asked and could not honour it or found a mismatch; 3 means the request was well formed and no browser existed to answer it.
contract.empty_registry: the registry ships empty and `--check all` therefore exits 1 today, printing that no measurement groups are defined. That is the designed answer, not an unfinished edge: a group states what a page SHOULD measure, which is a claim about a fix, and this binder fixes nothing. An empty registry that returned 0 would be a gate that passes by having nothing to check, which is precisely the failure mode the mode exists to prevent.
contract.preserves: everything measure-page-harness established. The document's three top-level keys are unchanged, the three state names are unchanged, the skip line is unchanged byte for byte, and exit 3 keeps its meaning. --self-test stays pure: the comparison logic is proven over synthetic reading maps and synthetic group tables carried in the script, so no browser is needed to prove that comparisons work.
contract.regression_risk: the failure to guard against is a vacuous pass — a gate that reports success because it compared nothing. Three shapes produce it and each is refused with its own exit: an unknown group name, a group with no expectations, and an empty registry under --check all. The second risk is the inverse: making a configuration fault report as a missing browser, which would let a typo in a group name read as “this machine has no browser” and be waved through. The ordering clause exists to keep those two apart and it is asserted.

oracle.command: uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --self-test && python3 skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --self-test && sh -c 'uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --check all; test $? -eq 1' && sh -c 'uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --check no-such-group; test $? -eq 1' && SHIM=$(mktemp -d) && ln -s "$(command -v uv)" "$SHIM/uv" && ln -s "$(command -v python3)" "$SHIM/python3" && env PATH="$SHIM:/usr/bin:/bin" sh -c 'command -v uv >/dev/null && command -v python3 >/dev/null && ! command -v playwright-cli >/dev/null' && sh -c 'env PATH="$1:/usr/bin:/bin" uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --check all; test $? -eq 1' _ "$SHIM" && uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test && uv run scripts/check_shared_copies.py --self-test && uv run scripts/sync_codex_agents.py --check && uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check
assertions: `--check <group>` runs the measurement, compares each reading against that group's expected value, and prints one line per comparison naming the selector, the property, the expected value and the measured value. It exits 0 only when every comparison holds and exits 1 on any mismatch — it never exits 0 having printed a complaint. The failing companion: a fixture group whose expected value differs from the fixture reading by one pixel exits 1, while its twin with the matching value exits 0.
an unknown group name exits 1 rather than passing vacuously, and says the name was not found. The failing companion is the same invocation with a real group name, which does not take that path.
a group whose expectation list is empty exits 1 rather than reporting that all zero comparisons held. The failing companion is a one-expectation group, which does not take that path.

`--check all` resolves every group in the registry, runs each, and exits 1 if any fails. Over an empty registry it exits 1 and prints that no measurement groups are defined — which is what it does in this repository today, because the registry ships empty. The failing companions: a fixture registry of two passing groups exits 0, and a fixture registry of one passing and one failing group exits 1.

the ordering is decided and proven: a configuration fault is resolved before the browser is probed. Under a PATH with no playwright-cli, `--check all` over the empty registry still exits 1 and not 3, because the registry is read first. The failing companion, in the same allow-listed browserless PATH: a --check naming a group that DOES resolve and has expectations exits 3 with the skip line, proving the two codes are chosen by the reason and not by which check happens to run first.

the skip line is unchanged: where exit 3 is reached through a --check invocation the harness prints `SKIPPED — no browser: playwright-cli is not on PATH, so no rendered geometry was measured and nothing below is proven` byte for byte, the same string measure-page-harness established, and claims no comparison in either direction.

--self-test stays pure — no browser, no network, no server subprocess — and covers the comparison logic, the three configuration faults, the ordering rule and each exit code over embedded synthetic reading maps and synthetic group tables. It exits 0 under a plain `python3 skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --self-test`.

the document measure-page-harness defined is unchanged: still the three top-level keys `run`, `states` and `probes`, still the three state names, still no wall-clock timestamp. The failing companion is a fixture asserting the earlier shape, which must still pass after this item's edit.
the regenerated Codex mirrors of measure_page.py under .agents/skills/ and plugins/karta/ are byte-identical to the canonical file, and `uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check` is clean.

signals: not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated.

contract mutation — this item fixes the exit-code contract later work gates on: 0 measured and matching, 1 asked and could not honour or did not match, 3 well formed and no browser. Changing any of those later would silently change what every future group means.
scope of impact — it edits the same canonical file measure-page-harness created, which is why that file is declared a shared resource here and the two items are sequenced rather than run together.
explicit — the empty registry means `--check all` exits 1 in this repository from the day it lands. That is intended and stated, and a reader who meets it should not read it as a defect.

work_items.title: Point it at the real page, and correct the runbook that tells you how
work_items.summary: Run the harness for real against the committed fixture at 1440x900, reach all three states, and write the runbook section that names the script, the command, the states, the exit codes and the skip line — replacing the instruction at line 28 that points an automated capture at a file:// URL the browser refuses.

contract.exposes: a section in docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md naming skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py by path, the command that runs it against the pinned fixture, the three state names, the three exit codes and the skip line quoted byte for byte — so a reader with no browser learns from the runbook what a skipped run does not prove, rather than only from the script's output.
contract.consumes: measure_page.py exactly as the two items before it built it. This item takes the first real reading, which is the first honest chance to find a defect in the instrument, so it may edit the script and its mirrors to fix what the run turns up. It declares them in touches for that reason. It adds no new mode and no new group.
contract.runbook_correction: docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md:28 currently says to open the design capture directly — “a `file://` path in a browser, or a `file://` `--design-url` if you are driving `capture_view.py`”. The first half is true for a person's own browser. The second half cannot work: capture_view.py drives playwright-cli (skills/karta-validate/scripts/capture_view.py:78 resolves it, :107 invokes it), and playwright-cli refuses that protocol outright — measured, and the refusal reads `Access to "file:" protocol is blocked`. The correction replaces that clause rather than sitting beside it: an automated capture must reach the file over http, served from the repository root, which is two levels above the design's own parent and therefore the lowest root from which its `../../skills/karta-status/assets/` references resolve. The runbook keeps saying that serve_design.py is the wrong server and gains the reason as a line cite: it roots the server at the design file's own parent (skills/karta-validate/scripts/serve_design.py:73), so those references 404. One paragraph is deliberately left alone — the run record at line 115 says a 2026-08-22 run opened the capture over file://. That is a record of what someone did, not an instruction to repeat it, and rewriting it would falsify the history.
contract.preserves: no page rule, token, theme or behaviour changes, and serve_status.py is not touched in any form. Nothing already in the runbook is deleted except the one clause the correction replaces: the four constants, the two clicks, the three intended differences, the five ruled-out differences and every recorded run stay exactly as they are. The measurement is read-only against the page.
contract.regression_risk: the pitfall here is a runbook that drifts from the script. The skip line is the string most likely to drift, because it lives in the script and is quoted in the prose, so its byte-for-byte identity is asserted with a failing companion rather than left to a careful reader. The second pitfall is the run itself reporting more than it saw: the fixture derives every work item as pending, so no halt badge, no running spinner and no part-filled progress bar can appear in it at all. What this run proves is that the instrument reaches all three states and returns real numbers — not that the page is correct, which nothing in this binder claims.

oracle.command: RUN=$(mktemp) && uv run skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py --root docs/designs/fixtures/watch-fidelity-state --viewport 1440x900 > "$RUN" && python3 -c 'import json,sys; a=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); assert sorted(a)==["probes","run","states"], sorted(a); assert sorted(a["states"])==["at-rest","binder-panel-open","card-detail-open"], sorted(a["states"]); assert all(v["reached"] for v in a["states"].values()), a["states"]; assert a["probes"] and all(set(("state","viewport","selector","computed","rect")) <= set(p) for p in a["probes"])' "$RUN" && grep -q skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md && python3 -c 'import importlib.util as u,pathlib,sys; sp=u.spec_from_file_location("mp","skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py"); m=u.module_from_spec(sp); sp.loader.exec_module(m); d=pathlib.Path("docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md").read_text(); sys.exit(0 if m.SKIP_LINE in d and all(n in d for n in m.STATES) else 1)' && grep -qF 'Access to "file:" protocol is blocked' docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md && ! grep -qF '`file://` `--design-url`' docs/conventions/watch-design-fidelity.md && uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test && uv run scripts/check_shared_copies.py --self-test && uv run scripts/sync_codex_agents.py --check && uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check
assertions: the harness is run for real against docs/designs/fixtures/watch-fidelity-state at 1440x900 and exits 0, and the document it prints has the three top-level keys `run`, `states` and `probes`, with `probes` non-empty and every probe carrying a getBoundingClientRect box. The failing companion: the same invocation against a root holding no binder must not exit 0 — it fails with a named reason rather than printing an empty document.

all three states are reached against the pinned fixture and each is reported reached true. The fixture binder derives as next and only the current binder's panel is open at rest (serve_status.py:3671-3673), so `binder-panel-open` requires the first click and `card-detail-open` the second; a run that reports either unreached fails this item rather than being recorded as a normal skip. The failing companion is a fixture run in which the second click is not taken, which must report `card-detail-open` unreached rather than reporting a reading for it.

the runbook gains a section naming skills/karta-status/scripts/measure_page.py by path, the command that runs it against the pinned fixture, the three state names, and all three exit codes with what each one means. The failing companion is the same check run against the pre-item file, which does not contain the path.

the skip line in the runbook is byte-for-byte the string the script prints, and so are the three state names. The check imports measure_page.py, reads `SKIP_LINE` and `STATES` off the module, and requires each to appear in the runbook — so the two copies cannot drift apart unnoticed and neither is ever hand-typed into the oracle. The failing companion: changing one character in either copy makes the check exit 1.

the instruction to point an automated capture at a `file://` URL is gone from the runbook's guidance, not merely qualified. Two exact checks say so, and both fail against the file as it stands today: the clause `` `file://` `--design-url` `` no longer appears anywhere in the file, and the measured refusal `Access to "file:" protocol is blocked` does appear. The correction names capture_view.py as the caller that hits the refusal, because it resolves and invokes playwright-cli (skills/karta-validate/scripts/capture_view.py:78 and :107), and it gives the route that works: serve the capture over http from the repository root, two levels above the design's own parent, which is the lowest root from which its ../../skills/karta-status/assets/ references resolve. The failing companion is the file as it stands, where that clause sits at line 28 and the refusal string appears nowhere.

the runbook keeps saying serve_design.py is the wrong server and now cites why: it roots at the design file's own parent (skills/karta-validate/scripts/serve_design.py:73). The failing companion is a version of the section that recommends serve_design.py, which must not pass.
the recorded run of 2026-08-22 at line 115 is unchanged. It describes what was done, and this item does not rewrite it. The failing companion is a diff that edits that paragraph, which fails review.

nothing outside the runbook's guidance changes. serve_status.py and its mirrors are untouched, no page rule or token moves, no entry in selftest_behaviours.txt is added or retired, and the whole floor is clean: `uv run scripts/validate_plugin.py --self-test`, `uv run scripts/check_shared_copies.py --self-test`, `uv run scripts/sync_codex_agents.py --check` and `uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check` all pass.

if this run turns up a defect in the instrument, the fix lands in this item's commit and the harness's own --self-test gains the case that would have caught it — so the repair is proven by a fixture and not only by the run that found it. If the run turns up nothing, no script edit is made and the touches entries for measure_page.py go unused, which is a legitimate outcome and not a gap.

signals: not-computed:sensitive — this repo configures no sensitive-path convention, so that signal could not be evaluated.

capability or resource escalation — this is the only item in the binder whose acceptance check actually opens a browser. On a machine with no node and no playwright-cli it cannot be gated at all, which is why node sits in this binder's runtime_contract and karta-build halts at preflight rather than letting this item fail as though the code were wrong.

contract mutation — it corrects a standing instruction in a convention document that other work follows. A reader who took the old advice was told to do something the tool refuses, so the correction is a behaviour change for people even though no code path moves.
scope of impact — it may edit measure_page.py, which the two earlier items own, so that file is declared a shared resource here and this item is sequenced last.
explicit — this item is what stops the instrument shipping unproven. Cutting it would leave a browser-measurement tool that has never been pointed at a browser.
